reference.raw: [1] Scott A. Mogull. “Accuracy of cited “facts” in medical research articles: A review of study methodology and recalculation of quotation error rate”. In: PLOS ONE 12.9 (Sept. 2017), pp. 1–17. doi: 10.1371/journal.pone. 0184727. url: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0184727.

sentences: Recent studies show that this link between claim and source is not always reliable: a citation may be present, yet the cited work may only partially support the statement, be interpreted incorrectly, or be used in a misleading way[1][2][3].
Mogull distinguishes between minor inaccuracies and major content errors[1].

First, Mogull[1] sharpens the definition of the problem by separating minor inaccuracies from major content errors, where the cited source fails to substantiate, is unrelated to, or contradicts the assertion.
Mogull[1] and Pavlovic et al.[2] operationalize citation inaccuracy differently even within the same research area, suggesting that inter-annotator agreement would itself be a significant challenge.

reference.raw: [2] Vedrana Pavlovic et al. “How accurate are citations of frequently cited papers in biomedical literature?” In: Clin Sci (Lond) 135.5 (2021), pp. 671–681.

sentences: Recent studies show that this link between claim and source is not always reliable: a citation may be present, yet the cited work may only partially support the statement, be interpreted incorrectly, or be used in a misleading way[1][2][3].
Pavlovic et al.[2] use a similar support-based criterion, identifying error types such as nonexistent findings, incorrect interpretation of results, and chains of repeated citation errors.

Second, Pavlovic et al.[2] provide empirical evidence that such claim-support problems do occur in published literature, finding at least one inaccurate citation in 11% and 15% of articles in their two datasets.
Mogull[1] and Pavlovic et al.[2] operationalize citation inaccuracy differently even within the same research area, suggesting that inter-annotator agreement would itself be a significant challenge.
